Stage a scaled entry, not one buy: first buy near $3.07 (the medium-term line), add near $2.94 (the short-term line), keep some dry for $2.84.
Set the exit target at $3.92, the 44-analyst average, only 14.62% above spot, so this is a quick trade, not a hold.
Protective stop at $2.80, just under the $2.8366 long-term line; below that the next floor is the $1.80 fifty-two-week low.
No earnings to trade around: Q2 2026 was reported Aug 11-12, so the binary risk is the Gram token price, which no date hedges.
Daily range is about $0.28, so a pullback to $3.07 or $2.94 is a normal one-to-two-day move, not a crash you must chase past.
agents.strongest: Chasing $3.42 after a 15% spike pays the top tick; wait and buy in tranches at $3.07 and $2.94 with a stop at $2.80 and a target of $3.92.

TONX.headline: TONX is a crypto treasury bet, not a business — skip it here.
rationale: Bear's point wins: the company's value tracks the Gram token, so this is one coin bet.
Risk Agent wins on math — about 15% up to $3.92 versus 47% down to $1.80.
I overrule Bull's 44-analyst buy rating; those targets sit barely above today's $3.42.
I also overrule Execution's staged-entry plan — a good ladder into a weak idea is still a weak idea.
Macro is right that today's 15% jump on double volume is money rotating, not a durable thesis.

CRML.name: Critical Metals Corp.

agents.name: Bull Agent
points: The two analysts covering it peg fair value near $13.00, about 83% above today's $7.12 price.
US government rare-earth funding just boosted its Greenland project, sending the stock up 29.5% on August 27.
An $835M merger with European Lithium has a September court date, a hard near-term catalyst.
Shares bounced hard off the $5.13 year-low and now sit above the recent $6.85 average, showing buyers returning.
Multiple 18-29% up days in late August show real money chasing the rare-earth government-tailwind story.
agents.strongest: A funded US-backed Greenland rare-earth project plus an $835M merger with a September court date give this a double-catalyst path toward the $13 analyst target.

agents.name: Bear Agent
points: CRML fell 11.44% today to $7.12, showing how fast the recent hype-driven gains reverse when sentiment cools.
The stock is still down 76% from its 52-week high of $29.97 and sits just above its 52-week low of $5.13.
The long-term trend is down: at $7.12 the stock trades below both its 50-day ($7.47) and 200-day ($9.75) average prices.
The entire rally rests on news, not profits: an $835M merger facing a September court date that could reject it, plus government funding hopes.
Only 2 analysts cover the stock, so the $13 average target is thin, low-conviction evidence.
agents.strongest: The whole move up rests on an $835M merger a court could reject in September, and today's 11% drop shows how quickly it unwinds.

agents.name: Macro Agent
points: Governments are pouring money into non-China rare-earth supply; CRML rose 29.5% on Aug 27 after US funding backed its Greenland project.
Allied demand is broadening: headlines show Japan eyeing Greenland rare earths and name CRML's Tanbreez deposit as strategically important.
Money is rotating into the whole group at once; on Aug 25 CRML, USAR and MP all climbed together on government support.
The theme has already been flushed of hype: at $7.12 the stock sits 76% below its $29.97 high, just above its $5.13 low.
Main headwind: this is a pre-production developer relying on an $835M merger with a September court date, and high rates make that financing risky.
agents.strongest: Western governments are actively funding non-China rare-earth supply, and CRML jumped 29.5% on August 27 when US money backed its Greenland project.

agents.name: Risk Agent
points: CRML swings about $0.70 a day on a $7.12 stock — nearly 10% — so any stop tight enough to protect cash gets hit by normal noise.
It dropped 11.44% in a single day today; anyone who bought yesterday is already deep underwater.
Down 76% from its $29.97 high and only about $2 above its $5.13 floor — break that and the loss is open-ended.
The case rests on one September court date that could reject the $835M merger — a yes/no event that can gap the stock overnight past any stop.
Price is below both the $7.47 and $9.75 average levels in a downtrend, with just 2 analysts behind the $13 target.
agents.strongest: A survivable stop here is more than 10% wide because of the daily swings, and a September court ruling can gap CRML straight past even that — the downside is uncontrollable.

agents.name: Execution Agent
points: No edge today: CRML fell 11.44% to $7.12, stuck between its $5.13 year-low and its $7.47 recent average price.
Better entry is a pullback to about $6.85, where the 20-day average sits and August buyers stepped in.
Binary event: the $835M European Lithium merger has a September court date that can approve or reject the deal outright.
Protective exit belongs just under $5.13, the year-low where the August bounce began.
Moves are violent (18-29% up days, an 11% down day), so any buy should be staged in thirds, not taken at once.
agents.strongest: The only hard catalyst is a September court ruling that flatly approves or rejects the $835M merger, so buy small on a dip near $6.85, stop below $5.13, and don't chase at $7.12.

CRML.headline: Real government tailwind, but a September court date decides it — wait, don't chase.
rationale: Macro's point wins: allied money is funding non-China rare earths, and CRML's Greenland deposit is named in it.
I overrule Bear's '76% below its high' argument — that damage is already in the price, not a fresh reason to avoid.
Risk wins on the honest part: one September court ruling can gap this stock overnight, past any exit.
Execution's read is right — today's 11% drop shows chasing spikes here loses money; the $6.85 area is where buyers showed up.
Bull's $13 target is thin at only 2 analysts, so I score the case on the catalyst, not the target.
dissent: If the merger clears in September, this runs before any patient buyer gets a calmer entry.
Government funding is real cash, not hype — waiting could cost the whole move.
Bear could be right that with no profits, a court rejection takes it back under $5.13.

sizing.note: Stop $5.72 (2x ATR, 19.7% below). Risking 1% of equity ($1) buys $3 — capped by dry powder.
